# ↪️ Pull Request

Fixes #4429.

## 💻 Examples

Before the entry detection served the first `index.html` bundle it found.

This would yield a 404 when running any other html file.

```
parcel serve test.html
```

I updated the logic, as suggested, to serve any single HTML entry.

## 🚨 Test instructions

I didn't see any tests for the dev server. Let me know if or where I can do so.

## ✔️ PR Todo

- [ ] Added/updated unit tests for this change
- [ ] Filled out test instructions (In case there aren't any unit tests)
- [X] Included links to related issues/PRs

But now I'm looking at existing tests I broke.

It seems all html bundles have `isEntry: true` although the tests in question run with a single entry filepath: `bundler('/integration/html/index.html')`. Would it be possible there is something else going wrong there?

> It seems all html bundles have isEntry: true although the tests in question run with a single entry filepath

isEntry mostly means: no hash.

For example:
https://parcel2-repl.now.sh/#

generates this bundle graph (a & b are "CLI entries", c is merely linked from a): 
![parcel2-repl now sh_](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4586894/82587554-b22fcc80-9b99-11ea-9d36-37261ba0be45.png)

I see.

> if there are 2 or more html bundles: 404 (because of the ambiguity, maybe the error page should state this as well)

Per suggest I updated logic from "serve first index.html" to "serve any single HTML bundle".

The problem is there are two tests failing with multiple HTML bundles where it serves a 404 now instead of the first `index.html` as before.

https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/v2/packages/core/integration-tests/test/server.js#L135
https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/v2/packages/core/integration-tests/test/server.js#L391

Both use the fixtures at `integration/html/` which contain both `index.html` and `other.html`. I hoped `isEntry` would filter out the other, but it doesn't. Not sure how to filter this correctly.

issue_context.title: 404 Page not found when serving arbitrary file
issue_context.body:
# 🐛 bug report

I'm trying to use Parcel 2 in no-config mode, for a very simple use case, serving a file named `test.html`. That fails with a 404 Page not found in the browser. There is no error shown anywhere.

## 🎛 Configuration (.babelrc, package.json, cli command)

node_modules/.bin/parcel serve test.html

## 💁 Possible Solution

Rename the file to `index.html`.

## 🔦 Context

I'm trying to serve different HTML files.

Must I create targets in `package.json`? I've read the README on that and it's not quite clear. For example, what does [dist/browser/index.js](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/v2/packages/core/parcel/README.md#target-configuration) represent? The [Sources](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/v2/packages/core/parcel/README.md#sources) section says at `1.` that specifying the file on the CLI should work.

## 🌍 Your Environment

<!--- Include as many relevant details about the environment you experienced the bug in -->

| Software         | Version(s) |
| ---------------- | ---------- |
| Parcel           | 2.0.0-alpha.3.2
| Node             | v13.11.0
| npm         | 6.14.3
| Operating System | Linux
comments:
This search for which bundle is served as the index https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/31c07ce8e81d808554fdbe51ef0ce3497accda5b/packages/reporters/dev-server/src/Server.js#L135-L152 should instead do: - if there are 2 or more html bundles: 404 (because of the ambiguity, maybe the error page should state this as well) - if there is only one html bundle: use that
> Must I create targets in package.json? No > For example, what does dist/browser/index.js represent? The output bundle (not input!) ```json { "main": "<>", "app": "<>", "source": "<>", "targets": { "app": {} } } ``` `parcel build path/to/package` (with `source` specified) and `parcel build <>` are equivalent.
How do you serve a html page inside a react app with parceljs? Was a solution proposed?
think it may be caused by the low version of node. I can solve the problem by upgrading node version to more than 16.0.0
